1.explanation: The Tab component’s render() builds the anchorProps with aria-posinset and aria-setsize, but it relies on a totalTabs prop. In the Tabs component’s render (in the tabsWithProps mapping), totalTabs is never passed into each cloned Tab, so Tab.props.totalTabs is undefined and aria-setsize isn’t set. To fix the VoiceOver announcement, Tabs.render must supply totalTabs (e.g. this.getTabs().length) when cloning each Tab so that Tab.render includes the correct aria-posinset/aria-setsize attributes.
1.bug_scenario: When navigating tabs with VoiceOver, each tab announces “1 of 1” instead of its position within the full set (e.g. “4 of 4”). In the demo, although the JSX example renders four tabs, the screen reader only hears the current tab as the lone item—indicating that the ARIA setsize/posinset attributes are never correctly applied.

2.explanation: VoiceOver relies on the ARIA properties aria-posinset and aria-setsize to announce “X of Y.” The Tab component’s render method correctly injects aria-posinset (index+1) and aria-setsize (totalTabs) into its anchorProps, but totalTabs is never passed in from the parent Tabs component. In Tabs.js, when we clone each <Tab> via React.cloneElement, we provide index, selected, handlers, and tabIndex—but omit totalTabs. As a result, Tab.props.totalTabs is undefined (falling back to 1), so aria-setsize is wrong and VoiceOver reads “1 of 1.” Fixing the bug requires: 1) updating Tabs.js’s render/cloneElement call to include totalTabs: this.getTabs().length, and 2) ensuring Tab.js’s render method applies ['aria-posinset'] and ['aria-setsize'] from its props so VoiceOver can announce the correct position and size.
2.bug_scenario: When navigating the Carbon React Tabs with VoiceOver, the screen reader always announces “tab, 1 of 1” regardless of the actual number of tabs. In the attached GIF you can see the fourth tab gets focused, but VoiceOver still says “1 of 1” instead of “4 of 4.”
